name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description: This degree prepares graduates of another discipline to teach it in high school. You study how teenagers learn, how to plan a unit and how to manage a classroom, then teach two of your subject areas on supervised school placements in each year. A final project looks at a question from your own practice.
units: Curriculum and Pedagogy in Your Teaching Areas

name: Master of Teaching (Early Childhood)
description: Learn to teach children from birth to eight, in early learning centres, kindergartens and the first years of school. Units on play-based learning, early literacy and numeracy and working with families sit beside placements in both settings. Much of the reading is tested against what you see children do.

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description: Already hold a degree in a school subject? Here you turn it into two teaching specialisms, with long blocks in Victorian secondary schools where a mentor teacher watches you plan, teach and reflect. Seminars cover research on learning, assessment and teaching students with a disability.
units: Learning and Teaching in Secondary Schools

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
description: A practical year for people who want to lead a room in a childcare centre. You plan play and learning experiences, keep children safe and healthy, and write the observations families and assessors read. Placement days in a centre run through the year.
units: Lead a Team in a Children's Service
